A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same RGR framework, key-query budget, constructions, and original experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-model experiments on permutation graphs, including capacity thresholds, head-count comparisons, scaling fits, and context-length sensitivity results in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the original capacity experiments and adds original softmax, value-retrieval, full Transformer, and denser-graph results in Sections 7 and Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The original max-over-heads construction is retained. Beyond v1's discussion of softmax, v3 specifies scaled per-head softmax followed by summation and thresholding, and implements additional configurations with frozen-value message retrieval and a full pre-LN Transformer block. These additions change inference operations, outputs, and training objectives.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates permutation-graph edge recognition. v3 additionally evaluates directed regular graphs with multiple neighbors, continuous value-message retrieval, and permutation-to-matching retrieval using frozen GPT-2 embeddings and a vocabulary selected using WikiText-103 frequencies. These introduce different task requirements and embedding populations.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same single-head versus multi-head comparisons. The new studies evaluate extensions of the paper's models, rather than adding competing published methods. Linear attention and MQA/GQA are discussed but not benchmarked; Figure 7's null outcome describes collapsed single-head runs.

E3.justification: The original protocol and Table 2 training cutoffs remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce an 80,000-step softmax budget, MSE-based value evaluation and stopping, and final-token accuracy for a Transformer trained up to 100,000 steps. Denser graphs use revised context construction and adaptive class weighting. The dedicated 16/32 train/test context-length protocol is removed.

E4.justification: Section 7 adds explicit robustness tests for softmax normalization, value routing, and a full Transformer with pretrained embeddings, including analysis of single-head training collapse. Appendix A.3 adds density sensitivity of capacity and optimal head count. Conversely, v1's context-length sensitivity study and Figure 8 are removed.

E5.justification: The original seed counts, 95% t-intervals, threshold intervals, and paired t-tests remain unchanged. New softmax and value experiments specify three runs, while the Transformer experiment specifies seven seeds and separately displays collapsed and converged single-head outcomes. This extends statistical reporting without establishing additional runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Original plotted results and scaling fits, including slope 1.19 with R2 = 0.944, are retained. New results include the denser-graph fit DK approximately 0.46 times (r m/dmodel) log2(m), value-retrieval MSE curves, and Transformer single-head outcomes near zero or 0.81 versus roughly 0.97 for four/eight heads at large budgets. These concern added settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions. Context-length results are removed.

T1.justification: v3 replaces v1's reduction of multi-head aggregation to a summed bilinear form with a direct max-over-heads Lipschitz/covering argument and an explicit bounded-norm qualification. Section 8 adds a scaled-softmax construction, lemmas, and guarantees with an extra logarithmic width factor and a minimum-context-length condition, replacing Appendix C's earlier same-budget treatment. However, the new proof does not establish the bounded-tail premise needed when applying Lemma 8.3 to exponentiated logits.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary expand from idealized QK capacity to a rationale claimed to persist with softmax, values, and a full Transformer using GPT-2 embeddings. v1's headline exact scaling is reframed as essentially m'/dmodel up to logarithmic factors, with distinct softmax guarantees. Density-dependent empirical scaling becomes a main contribution, while the empirical context-length-insensitivity claim is dropped.

C2.justification: v3 develops nonlinear competition as essential to the multi-head advantage, interprets density results as evidence for edge-based capacity, and links single-head collapse to optimization stability. Section 2.1 adds interpretations concerning trained LLMs and KV sharing. Limitations now discuss the unresolved softmax logarithmic gap and controlled single-layer scope, replacing several explicitly untested extensions in v1; the context-length interpretation disappears.

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial implementation information: regular-graph generation and adaptive weighting, frozen value-map construction, GPT-2 vocabulary selection from the first ten million WikiText-103 tokens, paired-slot encoding, tied unembedding, and Transformer architecture details. These document the added experiments rather than changes to retained runs. Some new settings, including the Transformer learning-rate value, remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially expands positioning relative to observed LLM behavior, including MQA/GQA, pruning, and linear versus softmax attention. Appendix D adds emergent sparsity and an extensive softmax-free attention discussion. New comparisons with Zhong et al. distinguish associative-memory retrieval from RGR and clarify the claimed novelty of demonstrating interference reduction in single-target tasks.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, contribution summary, model exposition, and limitations are substantially rewritten. Main-text construction summaries are shortened while their appendix treatments remain. QK/OV justification moves into the main exposition, and Appendix C is reorganized around computational footprint. The narrative now centers the multi-head rationale and its extensions.

P2.justification: v3 adds six result figures and a softmax algorithm display, while removing v1's context-length figure. Retained core plots are enlarged and redistributed, including figures previously placed side by side; appendix figures are relocated and renumbered. Tables 1–2 retain their contents. These are substantial display changes, beyond numerical updates or pagination.

improvement.justification: The added experiments substantially strengthen empirical support by addressing v1's explicitly untested denser graphs, softmax, values, and realistic embeddings. However, v3 elevates softmax guarantees to a central contribution while Section 8.1 applies Lemma 8.3 without establishing its required tail assumptions: sub-Gaussian logits alone do not imply uniformly sub-exponential exponentials. The context-length study is also lost. Substantial empirical gains therefore coexist with unresolved support for a broader central theoretical claim, preventing a reliable net overall-quality judgment.
